blindSummary: The country's uniform national framework applies to this state/province. The dossier found no incident-, ordinance- or enforcement-level evidence beyond the national LGBTQ-rights organisation's annual reporting for this unit, and this unit is not named in the reported 2024 or 2025 sub-national compilations; the record contains only the country-wide position.
blindSourceSummaries: Encyclopedia overview of LGBTQ rights in this country: the national legal timeline - recognition of same-sex unions and marriage in 2011 and 2013, adoption, discrimination protections, gender identity and expression (the March 2018 rulings allowing name/gender-marker change without surgery), conversion therapy, military service and blood donation, plus a section listing non-binary marker rules by federative unit. Framework is national; sub-unit variation is not covered by this page.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations legal throughout the country; legal gender recognition possible by self-determination; a 2019 ruling by the highest court prohibits discrimination and hate crimes on SOGI grounds; marriage equality since 2013 with active repeal efforts in the national legislature; the country continues to have one of the highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; 3,000+ openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections; a 2025 highest-court ruling allows nonbinary civil-registry amendments; the executive's pro-rights stance versus a conservative legislature has generated a surge of anti-LGBT+ proposals.

A domestic law-firm guide to LGBTQ+ legal rights for expatriates (updated April 2026): protections were established by the judiciary rather than statute - same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, joint adoption, name and gender-marker change without surgery, and criminalisation of homophobia/transphobia as equivalent to racism; major cities broadly welcoming with legal infrastructure accustomed to same-sex marriages and name changes; the guide states smaller cities and rural areas may present more social friction, though the legal rights are identical nationwide.
